title: Rafi Learns Bismillah
summary: Rafi learns the manners of eating: wash your hands, say bismillah, eat with your right hand, do not overdo it, and be grateful. (Bukhari and Muslim, from Umar bin Abi Salamah; QS. Al-A'raf: 31)
moral: Table manners: wash your hands, say bismillah, eat with your right hand, take just enough, finish it, then say alhamdulillah.
pages: That afternoon Rafi was busy playing. 'Rafi, come and have lunch, dear!' Mother called from the dining room. The smell of warm rice made Rafi's stomach rumble. He ran to the table.

Rafi sat right down and was about to take a spoonful. 'Wait a moment, dear,' said Mother gently. 'Your hands have been playing; wash them first to be clean.' Rafi blushed, then ran to the bathroom to wash his hands with soap.
Rafi sat down again. 'Before eating, we say bismillah,' Mother said. Rafi raised his hands and prayed, 'Allahumma baarik lanaa fiimaa razaqtanaa, wa qinaa adzaaban naar, bismillah.'

Rafi remembered the advice the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم taught a young boy: 'O boy, mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is near you.' (Bukhari and Muslim). So Rafi ate with his right hand, from the plate in front of him.
Feeling happy, Rafi took a great deal of rice. But his stomach quickly grew full, and there was still rice left on his plate. Rafi lowered his head. 'Oh, I took too much...'

'Allah says, Eat and drink, but do not be excessive,' said Mother (QS. Al-A'raf: 31). 'The rice left over is also a provision from Allah.' Rafi finished his rice little by little, and promised to take just enough next time.

After eating, Rafi and Mother said, 'Alhamdulillah, alladzi ath'amanaa wa saqaanaa wa ja'alanaa muslimiin.' Rafi knew: wash your hands, say bismillah, eat with your right hand, take just enough, then be grateful. The end.
